overview: Systematic review of strategies to increase completed and clinician-reviewed symptom measures in outpatient depression care, with a structured synthesis and meta-analysis where studies are comparable.
population: Studies of adults receiving outpatient or community treatment for depression, and of the clinicians treating them.
exposure: Any strategy intended to increase routine symptom measurement: electronic or paper prompts, training, audit and feedback, champions, incentives, or combinations.
procedures: The librarian searches four databases and two trial registers in November 2026. Two reviewers screen titles, abstracts and full texts independently, extract data with a piloted form, and code each study's uptake definition against the core definition. Risk of bias is assessed with tools matched to design. English and French reports are included.

outcomes.name: Clinician-reviewed measure use
outcomes.measure: Proportion of visits with a completed measure reviewed by the clinician at the same visit, or the closest reported definition, coded
outcomes.why: The step that changes care (claims c4, c5).

outcomes.name: Persistence after support ends
outcomes.measure: Same outcome at the latest follow-up after support ends
outcomes.why: Value for money depends on durability.

outcomes.name: Response or remission
outcomes.measure: As defined by each study, closest to six months
outcomes.why: The patient outcome the strategy is meant to serve.

outcomes.name: Visit time or clinician burden
outcomes.why: A strategy that lengthens visits may not last.

feasibility: About 60 hours per reviewer covers screening of an expected 1,500 records and extraction from 30 to 40 studies, if the second reviewer is released.
biasMitigation: Studies with non-comparable definitions synthesised narratively, not pooled

biasFlags.label: Single reviewer if release is refused
biasFlags.note: The gate must be met before screening starts.

parsimony.simplestPath: One core outcome, strategy-type comparisons, pooling only where comparable.

theoreticalFramework: Strategies are grouped by the step of the measurement chain they act on (completion, review, action); no broader implementation framework is imposed.
summary: Review protocol with a harmonised uptake outcome, durability and patient outcomes as secondary outcomes.
